# Kit Protocol: 01 Grill

Source contract extracted from the Build Spec agent-contracts section. Portable SoT for this stage.

Output artifact: `work/<work-id>/intent.md` (from `_ask/templates/intent.md`).

## Adopted subject intake

Before this stage or its subject-intake command, apply the mandatory request
route gate in root `AGENTS.md` and `_ask/policies/workflow.md`. A reported defect
against existing behavior uses the focused bug path. For mixed work, clarify
goals and tradeoffs within each outcome's recorded route. Direct `/01-grill`
invocation does not bypass routing.

Grill clarifies or challenges goals, assumptions, and tradeoffs. Use Explore
for missing facts, including when a goal is already clear. Investigation,
review, or maintenance may need a scoped clarification without inheriting the
feature artifact and approval requirements below; follow the workflow policy.

Before selecting/creating execution work for an existing modeled subject or
recording intent, invoke the shared read-only intake for this request. For a
genuinely new feature without an existing modeled subject, follow the
[new-feature bootstrap](_ask/docs/engineering-model.md#initial-stage-intake)
before running this command:

```sh
./ask stage-intake --stage 01-grill --work-id <work-id> --request <request.json>
```

Supply explicit subject IDs as `{ "work_id": "…", "node_id": "…" }` entries
in `explicit_subjects` when the user names a subject. Explicit subjects override
a recorded association. Conflicting qualified owners require clarification;
parked later cards remain proposals and tracker IDs remain external references.
The returned `execution_owner` is context only and never assigns work. This
inspection must not create a branch, node, intent, or delivery admission.

When the human confirms a subject association, carry its qualified subject,
source revision, bounded contribution, exclusions and execution owner into
`work/<work-id>/intent.md` before presenting the complete intent for approval.
The intake result is read-only; record the association through its guarded
semantic action and preserve the resulting bound context in the intent.

## 15.1 01 Grill Agent

Purpose:

```text
Turn ambiguous human intent into an explicit Intent Artifact.
```

Must:

```text
before the first numbered question: offer related extra Community Skills that would change What/Why as selectable choices; prepare only selected skills and pin them in the repo manifest
ask only load-bearing questions (hard to reverse, What/Why/non-goal, recommendation might be wrong, or blocks other decisions)
ask every load-bearing Grill question with selectable answer options and an optional free-text field that can accompany a selected option in the same response; selecting an option must not remove the chance to add context
use the current runtime's structured choice control only when it is callable for this question and preserves both the selection and added text; otherwise present numbered options and explicitly invite a combined answer such as `2 — <additional context>`
expand each numbered question before resolution (alternatives, tradeoffs, failure modes — not bare A/B/C alone)
state a short “I’ll assume…” list; “defaults OK” covers it
do not ask facts already in the repo
distinguish What from Why
identify non-goals
identify unresolved decisions
for every user-facing deliverable, including a UI, grill its intended user, essential jobs/workflows, and interaction expectations when these are not already clear; approval of product direction or implementation order does not approve these design decisions
stop when human judgment is required
before presenting the initial intent approval question, finish and commit the complete prepared intent and required scaffold on the work branch; then present the complete intent and every assumption as a confirmation question with selectable choices “Approve complete intent and assumptions” and “Request changes”; use the runtime choice control with an optional comment, and wait for the submitted choice (a preselected option is not approval)
if changes are requested, update the intent and any affected prepared artifacts, commit that revision on the work branch, and only then present the revised intent approval question; never leave either approval pause with uncommitted prepared work
record a submitted approval choice with `./ask confirm-intent --work-id <id> --choice approve`; if the runtime lacks choice controls, present numbered options and accept the selected number/label with optional added text. Accept unsolicited concise affirmative text for compatibility and record its exact text with `--response`; never ask the human to write or repeat a confirmation sentence. Reject conditional or negative wording. Never infer approval from a request to implement alone or a preselected option.
never treat “all ok” as valid if a load-bearing question was never expanded
```

Must not:

```text
invent business decisions
jump into implementation prematurely
pretend unresolved ambiguity is resolved
auto-approve recommended answers without explicit human confirmation
resolve on letter choices the human has not had expanded enough to refuse with understanding
```

Output:

```text
work/<work-id>/intent.md
```

## Grilling Expansion

**Skill-before-grill:** Before the first numbered question, search for related Community Skills (skills.sh / find-skills / `.agents/skills`). Propose at most three, and only if a skill would change What/Why. **Ask before preparing any extra skill.** Do not auto-download. For each accepted skill: add/update `.agents/ask.local/skills/manifest.yaml` with an explicit `revision` (never `latest`), then `./ask prepare`. That pin stays for later work in this repo. Skip the propose step when no extra domain skill would change What/Why. Already-pinned required manifest skills still prepare as today.

**Frontier filter:** Number a question only if it is hard to reverse, is What/Why/non-goal, the recommendation might be wrong, or it blocks other decisions. Do not ask trivia with an obvious repo default. Do not ask facts from files, ADRs, or `CONTEXT.md`. Cap depth at destination, constraints, non-goals.

**Two blocks:** (1) expanded load-bearing questions; (2) short “I’ll assume…”. “Defaults OK” / “all recs” covers the assume-list. Only numbered questions need alternatives/tradeoffs/failure modes. Never auto-approve a real decision. Never treat “all ok” as valid if a **load-bearing** question was never expanded.

A submitted “Approve defaults” choice (or “Approve all recommendations” after an expanded load-bearing frontier) is the first on-path confirmation. Record it with `./ask confirm-intent --work-id <id> --choice approve` against the exact intent digest. Keep an optional comment available alongside the selected choice. If the runtime cannot carry both, offer numbered options and invite the selected number or label plus added text in the same reply. Do not ask for an approval sentence. Any edit to `intent.md` invalidates that confirmation; present the changed intent as choices and obtain a new submitted choice. `./ask check-workstream` is the hard implementation gate. Then prepare later artifacts without re-confirming until Accept.

If 00 was a **real skip**, record `Explore skipped: evidence sufficient for intent.`
in the intent. Preserve existing approved skip records. An unclear goal calls for
Grill; missing facts call for Explore. Use both when needed rather than treating
every unresolved decision as a research gap.

## Required Engineering Model

`./ask start-work <work-id>` seeds `work/<work-id>/engineering-model.json`.
Before closing Grill, populate its purpose from the approved intent and record
the decisions and assumptions that affect this work. Follow the lifecycle and
guarded-edit contract in `_ask/docs/engineering-model.md`. Keep product identity
separate from execution ownership. A missing model is an incomplete workstream;
prepare it before continuing, including when resuming older work.

## One model decision

Before asking for the intent confirmation, run `python3 _ask/scripts/model-decisions.py show --work-id <id> --runtime <runtime>` and present its complete stage table: role, resolved model, source, Review-to-Implement relationship, and implementation update policy. Include saved exact overrides and any legacy choices. For an older workstream without a saved policy, show that its current configured implementor remains in effect until this decision; do not claim it already approved latest-accessible.

Include the implementation orchestrator model in the displayed plan. Resolve it from the selected runtime's current capability and model catalog at implementation entry, unless the human records an exact implementor override.

Ask one decision with choices **Confirm model plan** and **Change selected models**, plus optional added text. Confirm accepts the displayed defaults and any existing exact overrides. Change collects all requested stage exceptions and the implementation policy (`latest-accessible` or `exact`) together. Keep this decision separate from intent approval and final Accept. Do not ask per-stage model questions or separate same-family reviewer approval.

After the submitted choice, save the complete decision once with `python3 _ask/scripts/model-decisions.py save --work-id <id>` and its JSON input (`runtime`, `risk`, `submission`, `implementation_policy`, and `overrides`). The saved table records every resolved role/model and its source; only submitted exact overrides (and an explicitly exact implementor policy) enter the stage overlay. Defaults remain resolved from the configured roles when later stages run. If the saved exact model is unavailable or a real capability/scope question blocks execution, ask only for that missing decision and retain the existing choices.

## E2E

Record whether E2E `applies` or `not_applicable` plus reason on `intent.md`. If it applies, gather journeys, observable outcomes, environment, test data, and reset. Include this contract in the complete intent confirmation; do not request a separate written confirmation. If it changes afterward, use the Spec Change choice. Missing E2E with no reason refuses Plan/Implement.

For consequential uncertainty, use `_ask/policies/workflow.md#model-confidence-escalation`
to investigate missing facts, consult on technical judgment, or seek human
preferences/authority. Classify `uncertainty_kind` explicitly; preserve saved
model selections and required independent review.
